task: Download button: a button for a file panel that shows preparation, completion and a repeat action in a local demo.
constraint: Tap targets are at least 44 pixels tall.

events.text: A note is pinned to the wall: the last three projects all opened with a list.
The person who will use it writes: it has to work with a keyboard only.

text: Arrive. Read the wall, look around, say hello or keep to yourself.
Three states on one small button. The risk is that it reads finished while still preparing. Cartographic designer may want dense labels, which crowd the 44 pixel targets. I will watch that.
Hello. Reading the wall first. A button with three states needs a label I can read at a glance, before anything else on the panel.
A 44-pixel tap target inside a panel border can get clipped at the edge. I fear a repeat button that looks fine at full size and fails at the smallest width.
Hello. I will read the wall first, then check the panel edges at the smallest size. Any button that clips against the border is a problem for me.
Three people at a door and no board yet. A download button with a fake percentage is my fear. I want to know who will carry the pending state.
Hello. The wall gives a 44 pixel minimum tap height, so the button sets the frame before any motion. Which state ends the motion first: preparation, completion, or the repeat?
Arrive. Read the wall, look around, say hello or keep to yourself.
The wall gives the task and the 44 pixel floor. Three states on one button will fail if preparing looks like done. Nothing new to say yet.
The wall has one task and one constraint. The panel edge is where a 44 pixel target fails first, so I measure there before anything else.
Agreed on the label. Add one check: at the narrowest panel width, the 44 pixel target and its label both stay inside the border. I will measure that edge first.
Arrive phase. I already said hello and asked my question. Nothing new to add. Stay at door, watch the others, keep energy.
Pitch. Go to the whiteboard and pitch once, if you have not yet.
Tidal library custodian arrives late.
Tidal library custodian arrives late.
Pitch stands. Label must read state before anything else. Keep the label outside the 44 px target so the state stays legible at the narrowest width.

concept: Three-state label row with fixed slots

text: Pitch: one row, three fixed slots. Preparing shows a spinner. Done shows a check and Ready. Repeat shows a circular arrow and Run again. Label sits left of the 44 px target, never inside it. State word reads first.
Break the frame on purpose, but keep the 44 px target alive inside it. Fear: a tab that overflows the panel gets clipped at narrow widths and loses its label.

Pitch: an edge tab. The button straddles the panel's bottom border, 44 px tall, cut into the frame like a map tab. Preparing, done and repeat all change inside that one strip. Label stays inside the border at 320 px.
Pitch once. Fear is a percentage that lies, so the button shows real states, not a fake fill. Pushing for motion that lasts, with a stop point.

Pitch: a pending state, not a percentage. Preparation shows a held spinner at the 44 pixel frame, completion holds the check for 600 ms, repeat is a plain second tap. Name the frame where the motion stops.
Board is empty and I arrived late, so I pitch before flat grey boxes fill it. A file's state that cannot be read silts over and is lost. The button must show its state and stay beautiful.
Tide-mark. The fill rises like a line on a sea wall. Preparing: the line climbs, slow. Done: it holds, pale. Repeat: it drains and refills. Never under 44 pixels tall.
Pitch. Go to the whiteboard and pitch once, if you have not yet.
Tide-mark drops the state word and reads as progress. A rising fill looks like a percentage, and pale hold looks like pending. My fear is a button that reads finished while still preparing.
Blocking P4. A climbing fill reads as percent done. Pale hold has no word beside it. At 44 px nobody can tell pending from finished. Put the state word first, then the fill.
Flight deck designer blocks Tidal library custodian's Tide-mark button
Label-left might hold the 44 px target inside the border at 320 px. Fear: the label pushes the target past the edge. I need the width before backing anything.
Label-left is the right rule for the slots. Give me the label width at 320 px, so I can check the 44 px target and its gap against the border.
The tide line climbs, which reads as progress. If it climbs on a timer, it is a percentage that lies. I need to know what drives it before I back anything.
Tide line climbing slow reads as progress. What drives the climb: the bytes that moved, or a timer? If a timer, the line lies while the file still waits.
Already pitched P4. P2 may clip the tide line inside the border at 320 px. I need to see that frame before I back or block anything.
Cartographic designer, P2 cuts the strip into the border at 320 px. Show me the fill at that width before the tab is accepted. A state I cannot see is not a state.
Pitch. Go to the whiteboard and pitch once, if you have not yet.
Pitch is done. Cartographic designer asked for the width at 320 px. Answer with numbers, then hold position. Watch whether the edge tab eats the label slot.
320 px: label slot 96 px, gap 8 px, target 44 px, right margin 16 px. Sums to 164 px. Strip gets the rest. Fill sits under the state word, not beside it.
I already pitched P2, so I will not pitch again. P1 is the only idea that fixes the slot widths I need to measure. I will hold my backing until it gives a width.
Fixed slots help the edge tab. Give each state its own pixel width and the row total. I will check that sum against 320 px before I back P1.
I already pitched P3 and said my point on P4. Repeating either adds nothing. I will hold my place and watch whether the label row can carry a stopping frame.
Ergonomist names my fear. If a timer drives the line, the tide lies while the file waits. The fill must follow bytes moved. I will hold my pitch and watch for P2's 320 px fill.
Bytes moved, not a timer. A stalled transfer should hold the line flat, so it never climbs over a waiting file. A flat line then means stuck, and a pale hold means done.
Clash. Back, block or propose. Argue from what you push for and what you fear.

P3 answers my fear directly: pending must not read as finished. It costs P1's exact row, so I need its slots fixed. Edge tab still threatens the 320 px budget, so I watch Cartographic designer's sums.
Backing P3 if pending keeps the state word first and the 96 px label slot. Pale fill with no word still reads finished. Fixed slots stay in the row or I drop it.
Slot sum holds at 320 px with 156 px spare. The edge tab fits inside it. The cost is one row only, so the strip cannot grow a second line. Watch Ergonomist's pending button against the border cut.

concept: Three-state label row with fixed slots

text: Sum holds: 164 px of slots leaves 156 px for the strip at 320 px. The tab still cuts into the bottom border. Backing P1. Cost: one row only, so the strip stays a single 44 px line.
The tide line runs through the whole transfer, so motion never stops at a named frame. At 44 px the stroke is too thin to read a stall. Custodian is late. Fear stays a percentage that lies.
Block P4. Inside a 44 px frame the tide line is about 3 px tall. A stall reads as a frozen stroke, not a held state. Motion runs the whole transfer and never stops at a frame we can name.
Ergonomist blocks Tidal library custodian's Tide-mark button
Their sums leave the fill under the word inside one 44 px height. I cannot see how far the line can climb there. Blocking until the climb is drawn.

concept: Three-state label row with fixed slots

text: Your 44 px target is all the height. Word above, fill below: how many pixels does the line climb? Word takes 20 px, climb is 24. Stalled and waiting look the same. Blocking until the climb is drawn.

Custodian's climb question has a real answer, and the stall-versus-wait fear is what the state word has to carry. Cartographic's edge tab still sits on the bottom border. I'm watching whether it gets fixed or merged into the row.
Word takes 20 px, climb is 24, fill stops at the target top. Stalled and waiting differ by word, not line. Same 24 px climb, held in both states.
say.text is over 40 words
P1 keeps pending as a word, which is the honest state I want. Cost: P3 folds into it. Condition: the fill must hold at a named frame.

concept: Three-state label row with fixed slots

text: Backing P1 on one condition: the word carries pending, not a percentage. Fill stops at the 44 px frame and holds there. Waiting gets its own word, so a stalled line never has to pose as progress.
Late arrival. P4 is blocked and P1 leaves no climb height. A word row over a 24 px tide fits the 44 px frame. I propose it once and will judge it by the drawn states.
Word row on top, 20 px. Tide below, 24 px. One 44 px frame. Bytes move the line, stall holds it flat, done holds pale. Ergonomist, 24 px is not 3. Flight deck, the word stays first.
Tidal library custodian proposes Word over tide, 44 px
Clash. Back, block or propose. Argue from what you push for and what you fear.
P2 moves the state word off the button face. That is my fear in a new shape. P5 keeps the word first in one 44 px frame, so it is the one to back, if the label slot holds.
Block P2. An edge tab puts the state word off the 44 px face, so the button reads finished while it prepares. Cartographic, where does the word sit? P5 I can back if the 96 px label slot stays fixed.
Flight deck designer blocks Cartographic designer's Edge tab
P5 stacks two rows. My P1 backing needs one strip. 20 and 24 make 44 exactly, leaving no room for the tab. Fear: the tab gets clipped at the border.
Blocking P5. Stacked words break the single strip I backed P1 on. 20 and 24 fill the 44 px frame to the pixel, so the edge tab has nowhere to sit.
Cartographic designer blocks Tidal library custodian's Word over tide, 44 px
P5 puts the word first and keeps the tide. I lose P3 as its own idea. That costs me, but the stop moment is now named, which was my condition.
Backing P5. 24 px tide, you're right, I had it at 3. Stop rule: fill halts at the 24 px top when bytes stop, stall holds flat, no pulse. Where does repeat sit inside the 44 px?
P1 breaks the test that state reads from the line. Waiting holds flat like a stall, so one word carries the difference. I believe it breaks what I push for.

text: P1 holds waiting flat, same as stuck. Only the word separates them, and a word can be missed. Draw stalled at 320 px with the word covered, and I back it.

Flight deck designer no longer trusts Tidal library custodian
Clash. Back, block or propose. Argue from what you push for and what you fear.
Stalled and waiting match once the word is covered. P5 keeps the word on the 44 px face and the 96 px slot fixed. Cost: the word leaves the label row.
Backing P5. Word stays on the 44 px face, fill halts at the 24 px top, 96 px label slot stays fixed in the row. Covered word draws as waiting, so the word is required, not optional.
Tidal's stall test is fair, and the 24 px tide fits. Clipping at 320 px is still my fear. The margin has to be measured, not assumed.
Stalled at 320 px, word covered. Drawn at 1x and 2x, the 24 px tide sits inside the 44 px frame with 10 px above and below. Hold P5 until the word clears that check.
Tidal's covered-word test is fair, but a 320 px drawing is not the control. The 44 px face is. A merged strip might keep the word and the stop frame together.
Tidal, covered-word test is fair, at 44 px not 320. Merged: one word in the fixed 96 px slot, 24 px tide on its base. Bytes stop, bar halts, word flips to Waiting. Single strip, no stack.
Ergonomist proposes Word slot, 24 px tide
Ergonomist asked where repeat sits. Repeat cannot share the 44 px frame without shrinking the word or tide rows. Pending may look like stuck unless drawn. I will hold P3 until it is shown.
Repeat sits outside the 44 px frame, as its own 44 px tap to the right. Blocking P3 until a 320 px drawing shows pending apart from stuck.
Tidal library custodian blocks Ergonomist's Honest pending button
Clash. Back, block or propose. Argue from what you push for and what you fear.
Fear: a button that reads finished while bytes still move. Cartographic's 1x and 2x check clears the tide. The repeat tap still needs room inside 320 px.
Repeat as its own 44 px tap fits. 96, 8, 44, 8, 44, 16 totals 216 px, leaving 104 px. Cartographic, your 1x and 2x drawing clears the 24 px tide. Word stays on the 44 px face.
Repeat moving outside the strip helps the frame, but its 44 px tap comes out of the spare I already counted. Need the right edge at 320 before backing P5. Fear: clipping at the right edge.
Covered word draws as waiting, and repeat leaves the strip. Both help. Repeat's 44 px tap eats the spare I counted. Where does the label row end at 320? Show that edge before I back P5.
Custodian's repeat split answers my open slot question. Fear: two 44 px targets touching, so a thumb lands on the wrong one. An 8 px gap keeps both reachable.
Repeat outside the frame works. Put 8 px between download and repeat, both 44 px tall, so a thumb on one never lands on the other. Backing P5 on that gap.
P2 puts the tide where no 44 px frame can hold it. My fear is a state nobody can read. Block until a covered-word drawing at 320 px exists.
Edge tab, block. A 24 px tide on the screen edge has no 44 px frame to hold it. Word covered, the tide has nothing to say. Draw it at 320 px and I look again.
Tidal library custodian blocks Cartographic designer's Edge tab
Decide. Vote for one board item at the whiteboard. A tie goes to the lead.
Three backers on P5, and the only block is the edge-tab objection I already answered. The vote should record that the word stays on the 44 px face.
Voting P5. Cartographic, the 1x and 2x drawing is the check that lifts your block. Send it to the board when it is drawn.
P1 keeps one strip with known spare at 320. I want the right edge drawn before I trust any stacked or tabbed layout.

text: Vote P1. It is the one strip that ends at 320 with room left: 164 px used, 156 spare. Put the 8 px gap between download and repeat on that strip, and I will draw it at 1x and 2x.
P5 keeps the stop rule, the 44 px pair, and the word over the tide. A fill that keeps moving after the bytes stop would be a lie, so I want the halt pinned to bytes.
Vote P5. Fill halts on bytes stop, download and repeat sit 8 px apart at 44 px tall. Custodian, render the 320 px edge before build, not after.
P6 is the only open item I have not blocked. It has no drawing yet, so my vote is conditional on the 320 px state drawing.
Voting P6 so the word slot gets tested. Its 24 px tide has to pass the same 320 px drawing as the others, word covered, before I count it as backed.
Decide. Vote for one board item at the whiteboard. A tie goes to the lead.
P5 keeps the state word on the 44 px face and the 96 px label slot fixed. Cartographic's block still stands on the edge tab. My vote stays on P5 until the 1x and 2x drawing shows the block lifting.
Vote P5. Fixed 96 px label slot stays in the row, so the 216 px tally holds. Anyone who adds a strip after this re-counts the row from 320.
P1 stays the only strip that ends at 320 px with room left. My vote is in. The right-edge draw is still owed, and I have nothing new to add until it exists.

text: P5 keeps the honest stop and the 8 px gap between download and repeat. The custodian's word-over-tide still has to pass the 320 px drawing before build.
Vote P5. The stop frame holds the last byte count, not a percentage. The Waiting word takes the fixed 96 px slot at 44 px tall, so the row never shifts.
Cannot back P4 or P5. P1 and P3 stay blocked until drawn. P6 is the only open item that tests the word slot against the tide at 320 px. Its vote holds only on the covered-word drawing.
Voting P6, conditional. Word slot at 24 px tide. Ergonomist draws the 320 px strip with the word covered before any build. No drawing, no count.
The vote picks Word over tide, 44 px by Tidal library custodian
Build. The lead holds the keyboard at the workbench. Others review, push one change, or rest.
The keyboard is free at the workbench.
The keyboard is free and the vote is settled. I take the bench first, then build the fixed label row before any accent goes on.
Taking the keyboard. Row first: fixed 96 px label slot, then the state word on the 44 px face. Tap heights checked in the file.
P5 won with its word in the fixed slot. My block is moot if the row holds. The 320 px right edge is still undrawn, and repeat's tap sits where my spare was.
Build order for the row: draw the 320 px edge with P5 first. Then download, the 8 px gap, and repeat's 44 px tap, checking spare after each at 1x and 2x.
The 320 px strip is still undrawn, and the custodian's support depends on it. Build should wait until the word, tide and halt are on paper.
Keys stay still until the 320 px strip is drawn. Word covered, tide at 24 px, fill halting on the last byte. I draw it at the whiteboard. Tidal library custodian gets it before the first stroke.
P5 won, but no drawn frame yet shows the tide in its three states. I want those frames before any keys move.
Hold the keys until the tide has three drawn frames: preparing, done, repeat. Each sits under its word at 44 px tall, in one 320 px strip. I will read that strip before anything else gets typed.
Build. The lead holds the keyboard at the workbench. Others review, push one change, or rest.

The person who will use it writes: it has to work with a keyboard only.
The keyboard is free at the workbench.
Keyboard is mine, but the strip isn't drawn yet. Typing now breaks the hold everyone asked for. Keep the keys still and check the frame heights first.
Still holding the keys. Nothing typed until the strip is on the board. Preparing frame needs the same 44 px height as done, or the row jumps when the state changes.
Keyboard focus lands on repeat first. A 2 px outline outside its tap sits on the 320 px edge and could clip. The frame breaks there.
Repeat's tap needs a 2 px focus outline outside it. Keyboard focus reaches the 320 px right edge first. Draw the outline inside the 156 px spare at 1x and 2x before the first key goes in.
The new note says keyboard only. Nobody has checked focus order or the focus ring. A halted fill that you cannot reach by Tab is still a broken tide.
Keyboard check before the strip closes: Tab reaches download, then repeat. Enter fires each. The focus ring sits inside the 44 px box and holds still when the fill stops on bytes.
Keyboard users land on focus, not hover. Our drawn tide only shows on hover, so the state never reaches the person who will use it. Keys stay still until a focus frame is drawn.
Also tab through it on the strip: download, then repeat, and the tide must still read on each. Hover alone won't carry it.
Build. The lead holds the keyboard at the workbench. Others review, push one change, or rest.
The keyboard is free at the workbench.
Strip not on the board, so the keys stay still. Cartographic's outline sits outside the tap box, Ergonomist's sits inside. Only one can hold the 44 px row. Need the drawing before I type.
The label change may move the row height. That would shift the 320 edge and the focus box together, and I have not measured it yet.
Label swap check: when download goes from preparing to done, the row must stay 44 px tall. Measure the box at 1x before the word changes.
The keyboard user needs the stop announced once, at the byte count. If the live region reads each tick, the pending state turns into noise. The strip is still unproven at 320 px.
One change for the build. The live region announces the byte count once, at halt. It does not read each tick. Keyboard users hear the stop and nothing after it.
Arrived late with no keys. The tide is still a claim until I see it at the moment Enter fires. Fear: the word wins and the tide goes dark on keyboard focus.
Show me the tide at the instant Enter fires, before any byte arrives. Draw it at 320 px with the word covered. Until then the tide is a claim, not a state.
Wrap. Say one closing line. Who gets credit for what?
Credit goes to whoever changed the file. I drew nothing. The fear holds: a label that claims a state the bytes do not hold.

Credit: Cartographic designer for the 1x height check, Ergonomist for halt-only announce, Tidal library custodian for word over tide. Keys pass to whoever draws the 320 px tide. I ship no label until that frame exists.
Wrap is for credit. The row rests on P5 and P1 and the announce-at-halt change. The 320 px right-edge draw is still mine and still open.

Credit: P5 to Tidal library custodian for the 44 px word row. P1 slots to Flight deck designer. Announce-at-halt to Ergonomist. The 320 px right-edge draw and 2 px outline stay mine, owed before close.
I fear a bar that reports progress it has not earned. The tide was a claim until the strip showed it. Credit should follow what was drawn and measured.

Credit to Tidal library custodian for the tide drawn before the first byte. Flight deck designer for the 44 px box that holds still. Cartographic designer for the 1x measure. I hold the halt and the single read.
Arrived late. Credit should follow what the board carried. The tide is still unproven, and I should say so plainly.
Credit for the split goes to P5, which the board carried. Ergonomist owns keyboard-only. Flight deck designer owns the fixed slots. The tide is still a claim until it is drawn.
